name: MAX16051ETI+
title: MAX16050/MAX16051: voltage monitor and power sequencer with reverse sequencing, 2.7 V to 16 V, 28-pin TQFN
summary: A power sequencer and supervisor that turns a board's supplies on one after another through open-drain enable outputs, checks each rail against an adjustable 0.5 V threshold, and releases a reset once all are good. On SHDN it switches them off in reverse order, draining each rail with an 85 mA pull-down until it is under 250 mV before the next goes; on a fault all go off at once. An overvoltage flag, a bus-removal flag, a charge pump for n-channel pass switches and a chaining scheme for more rails are included. The MAX16051ETI+ watches six voltages and sequences five in a fixed order; the MAX16050ETI+ watches five and sequences four in an order picked by three pins.
key_figures: 0.7 mA typ, 1.4 mA max at VCC = 3.3 V
128 ms typ (50 to 300 ms) with TIMEOUT on ABP, or set by a capacitor
VCC + 5 V typ, 25 µA typ source
MAX16051: 6 monitored, 5 sequenced; MAX16050: 5 monitored, 4 sequenced

notes: + marks a lead-free, RoHS-compliant package; EP is the exposed pad.

pins.name: GND

pins.name: ABP
pins.function: Output of the internal regulator that runs the chip; takes a 1 µF capacitor to GND and can supply more than 1 mA to outside circuits.

pins.name: EN

pins.name: DISC4

pins.name: CP_OUT
pins.function: Charge-pump output at about VCC + 5 V, sourcing up to 25 µA, for pulling up gates of external n-channel MOSFETs.

pins.name: EP

circuits.title: Sequencing four DC-DC converters
circuits.description: Four DC-DC converters run from VBUS, each enabled by one OUT_ pin that a resistor pulls up to VBUS. Each converter output is watched by a SET_ divider and tied to its DISC_ pin, so the chip can both confirm it has come up and drain it on the way down. VBUS also feeds VCC and, through a divider, EN, so the whole sequence waits for the input rail. SEQ1 to SEQ3 are left open for the default order OUT1, OUT2, OUT3, OUT4; EN_HOLD is tied to ABP; capacitors on TIMEOUT and DELAY set the reset timeout and the step delay. RESET, OV_OUT, FAULT and REM are pulled up to VPU, and an LED on REM shows when the board must not be unplugged.

circuits.title: Setting a SET_ input threshold
circuits.description: A two-resistor divider from the supply being watched to ground feeds one SET_ input; R1 and R2 fix the supply voltage at which the input crosses 0.5 V. VCC runs from VBUS and RESET reports the result.
notes: SET1 stands for any of SET1 to SET4 (SET5 on the MAX16051); the circuit is the same for each.

circuits.title: Two devices daisy-chained for eight supplies
circuits.description: Two MAX16050s each sequence four DC-DC converters wired as in the four-converter circuit. U1 starts first; its RESET drives U2's EN node, so U2 begins only when all four of U1's rails are good. Pulling the shared SHDN line low starts the power-down: U2 turns its rails off in reverse order, and its REM, tied to U1's EN_HOLD (pulled up to U1's ABP), keeps U1 on until every U2 rail has fallen below VTH_PL; then U1 powers its own rails down. All FAULT and OV_OUT pins share one line, so a fault or overvoltage on any rail shuts all eight off together. U2's RESET is the system reset.

parts.note: U1 EN_HOLD pull-up to U1 ABP

parts.value: SHDN (low starts reverse shutdown of all 8 supplies)

notes: Nets prefixed A belong to U1, B to U2.

circuits.title: Three DC-DC converters and a MOSFET switch in sequence
circuits.description: As the four-converter circuit, but the fourth rail is VBUS switched through an n-channel MOSFET. Its gate is OUT4, pulled up to CP_OUT, which sits about 5 V above VCC, so the MOSFET is fully on once OUT4 releases. V4 is watched by SET4 and drained through DISC4 like the converter rails.

operation.text: The MAX16051 watches six voltages (five SET_ inputs plus EN) and sequences five, always in the order OUT1 to OUT5. The MAX16050 watches five and sequences four; its three-level SEQ1 to SEQ3 inputs pick one of 24 orders, and all three open gives OUT1 to OUT4.

All OUT_ pins stay low until four things hold together: ABP is above the undervoltage lockout, EN is above its threshold, SHDN is high, and every DISC_ pin is below 250 mV. Then the first OUT_ releases. Each next OUT_ releases once the previous rail's SET_ input passes its threshold plus the DELAY time (10 µs with DELAY open). A rail may take as long as it needs to come up; the chip simply waits. When the last rail is good RESET releases after the reset timeout.

Once sequencing is done, any SET_ input falling under its threshold is a fault: every OUT_ goes low at once, RESET goes low, all DISC_ pull-downs turn on, and FAULT is driven low for at least 1.9 µs. The chip then starts again as soon as the four start-up conditions hold.

SHDN low turns the rails off one at a time in the reverse of the power-up order. Each OUT_ goes low, its DISC_ pin sinks 85 mA, and once that DISC_ pin reads under 250 mV the following OUT_ is switched off straight away, with no capacitor delay. SHDN is pulled up to ABP inside and must be low for the minimum pulse width before the chip acts.

EN falling under its threshold turns all rails off together without reverse sequencing. RESET goes low at once on either SHDN or EN, and REM releases when every DISC_ pin is below 250 mV. If SHDN has already gone low, a later fall of EN is ignored; for an EN shutdown, SHDN has to stay high for tENLO_OUT after EN falls, otherwise a reverse-order shutdown may start instead.

As VCC falls below about 2.2 V typ, ABP drops under VUVLO; from then on DISC_, OUT_ and RESET are held low as long as VCC is above VCCR (1.1 V max), and below VCCR their state is undefined. FAULT becomes undefined as soon as ABP is under VUVLO.

CP_OUT behaves like a 25 µA current source that climbs to VCC + 5 V. It can pull up the gates of one or more n-channel pass MOSFETs; a capacitor from gate to ground sets the turn-on slew. Pull-up resistors from CP_OUT to OUT_ pins that are still low draw current from it, which can pull CP_OUT down far enough that other MOSFETs are not fully enhanced.
Tie an unused SET_ input to ABP and that channel's DISC_ to GND; neither may float. Disabling one channel leaves the others working.

FAULT has a 100 kΩ pull-up to ABP. With EN and SHDN high it goes low when any SET_ input drops under threshold. Pulled low from outside for at least tFAULT_PW it shuts every OUT_ off at once. FAULT pins of several chips can be joined so a fault anywhere shuts every chip down together, pull-downs included.

OV_OUT, open-drain, goes low when any SET_ input exceeds 0.55 V and releases after a short delay once all are back below. It does not turn the outputs off by itself; to make an overvoltage force OUT_ low, OV_OUT is wired to FAULT.

Each DISC_ pin goes on its sequenced rail. It is high impedance in normal running; when its OUT_ goes low it sinks 85 mA to drain the rail's capacitors below 250 mV so the next rail can be switched off, and it senses the rail during reverse sequencing.

REM is low while any DISC_ pin is above VTH_PL and released once all are below it, marking when the input power may be removed after a controlled power-down. An LED on REM can show when it is not yet safe to pull a board.
While EN_HOLD is low a falling SHDN or EN is ignored; it must be high for either to turn the chip off. It is used to chain chips; tie it to ABP when not needed.

Several chips can be chained. Joining all FAULT pins turns every supply off on any fault. In the two-chip circuit, U1's RESET drives U2's EN so U2 sequences after U1; for power-down SHDN is pulled low, U2 shuts its rails off first, and U2's REM, held low while any U2 rail is up and tied to U1's EN_HOLD, keeps U1 on until U2 is done.
The SET_ input leaks up to 100 nA, and the error this adds to the trip point grows with the divider resistance. Smaller resistors cut the error and raise the divider's power draw.
The open-drain outputs are rated for 0.3 V low at 3.2 mA with VCC = 3.3 V, so the pull-up must keep the sink current under that: more than 1.6 kΩ to a 5 V pull-up rail, more than 3.74 kΩ to 12 V.

A pass MOSFET sits in series with its supply, so its on-resistance times the load current sets the voltage lost. Choose its RDS(on) for a gate-source drive of 4.5 V to 6.0 V (see Recommended MOSFETs).

Decouple VCC with 0.1 µF and ABP with 1 µF, each to GND and each right beside the chip. Solder the exposed pad to the ground plane for heat, and connect GND as well; the pad is not to be the only ground.
